rationale: The camera is the oldest model and stopped connecting after an overnight base station update, while the rest of the system remains fine. Repeated re-pairing attempts fail, which aligns with a protocol conflict between the old peripheral firmware and the updated base station firmware.

output.symptom_summary: Oldest camera cannot connect after base station update; re-pairing fails three times; other devices unaffected.
output.suspected_root_cause: Protocol conflict between old camera firmware and updated base station firmware.
key_abnormal_indicators: Issue started immediately after base station update
Only the oldest camera is affected
output.customer_reply: Thank you for the details. Since the issue started right after the base station update and only affects your oldest camera, it is likely a compatibility conflict between the camera's older firmware and the new base station firmware. We will need to check for a firmware update for the camera or perform a compatibility fix. Our advanced support team will assist you further.

complaint: My office camera no longer connects since the overnight base station update. I've tried to re-add it three times and each time it says it can't connect. It is the oldest camera I have, from the first package three years ago. The rest of the system is fine, so I'm hesitant to blame the update.
usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, and it summarizes the symptom accurately. However, actionability is weak: it only says the advanced support team 'will assist' and vaguely mentions checking for a firmware update or compatibility fix, without concrete steps the customer can take. It also implies a diagnosis (protocol/firmware conflict) without any checks shown as completed in the session record, which contains no questions asked or actions performed. It avoids claiming fixes were done, but the root-cause assertion is unsupported by evidence.
